fact: The mayor of Libreville said on 3 July 2026 that the city already has its own operational system digitalising municipal revenue and securing collection, developed with the public Treasury; the document names no other local government with such a system.

A consultancy (Manager General Consulting) presented the Colloc-Pay platform to the Ntoum commune and the Komo-Mondah departmental council on 2026-06-19; no adoption is stated, and the platform is described as digitising and geolocating operators, digitising communal assets and enabling electronic payment of taxes.

The commune of Owendo signed an agreement with the Direction générale des Impôts on 2026-04-29 to implement the national Digitax application for municipal taxes; implementation is announced, one commune named.
Digitax is the Direction générale des Impôts' platform; the DGI will align the Owendo municipal agents' taxpayer directory with its own and parameterise the forms, per the 2026-04-29 agreement.
Owendo and the DGI signed the Digitax partnership on 2026-04-29, with payment by bank transfer and mobile money and automatic taxpayer certificates planned.
The Libreville city hall launched a pilot of digitised municipal revenue collection on 2025-07-29; one commune is named.

The pilot platform is described as resting on a geolocated taxpayer file, online declaration and payment, automatic tax and penalty amounts and a dashboard showing who is up to date on which taxes; these are the vendor's stated design at launch, 2025-07-29.
The platform is developed by the company GTI Gabon, inspired by the national Digitax platform, for the Libreville city hall; launched 2025-07-29.
Libreville launched the revenue-digitalisation pilot on 2025-07-29.
